items.title:
Anthropic has filed for an IPO, with its prospectus revealing just how fast the company is scaling.
FY25 revenue jumped 1,088% YoY to $4.59B, while compute and infrastructure spending rose 190% to $7.33B.
The company posted an $8.06B operating loss and ended 2025 with $20.28B in cash and short-term investments.
Anthropic’s two largest direct customers accounted for 24% of total revenue combined.
items.title_ja:
Anthropic は IPO を申請しており、その目論見書により同社がいかに急速に拡大しているかが明らかになりました。
25 年度の収益は前年比 1,088% 増の 45 億 9000 万ドルとなり、コンピューティングとインフラストラクチャへの支出は 190% 増の 73 億 3000 万ドルとなりました。
同社は80億6000万ドルの営業損失を計上し、2025年終了時点では202億8000万ドルの現金と短期投資を残した。
Anthropic の 2 つの最大の直接顧客は、合計収益の 24% を占めました。

items.title:
Wonder is exploring a sale of food-delivery business Grubhub, the Wall Street Journal reports. Bankers have contacted Walmart, Target, Kroger and other retailers about a deal, according to sources.
Wonder, the food-hall startup led by Marc Lore, agreed in 2024 to buy Grubhub from Just Eat Takeaway for $650 million. Just Eat had paid $7.3 billion for it in 2021.
items.title_ja:
ワンダーは食品配達事業グラブハブの売却を検討しているとウォール・ストリート・ジャーナルが報じた。関係者によると、銀行家らはウォルマート、ターゲット、クローガー、その他小売業者と取引について接触しているという。
マーク・ロア氏率いるフードホールの新興企業ワンダーは、2024年にジャスト・イート・テイクアウェイからグラブハブを6億5000万ドルで買収することで合意した。ジャスト・イートは2021年に73億ドルを支払っていた。

items.title:
Databricks is in early talks to raise funding at a $225 billion valuation, the Wall Street Journal reports.
The new financing would be a nearly 20% increase from the data and AI company's August valuation.
items.title_ja:
データブリックスは2,250億ドルの評価額で資金調達に向けて初期交渉を行っているとウォール・ストリート・ジャーナルが報じた。
新たな資金調達は、データ・AI企業の8月の評価額から20％近く増加することになる。

items.title:
GTCR says in a 13D filing that it may submit a proposal to acquire additional or all shares of Global Payments, backing Bloomberg's report of a possible $50 billion buyout.
GTCR holds 43.3 million shares (16.35%), about $4.0 billion at today's $91.83 close. It received the stake in the January Worldpay deal. No proposal has been made and no decision has been taken.
items.title_ja:
GTCRは13D提出書類の中で、500億ドルの買収の可能性があるというブルームバーグの報道を支持し、グローバル・ペイメンツの株式を追加または全株取得する提案を提出する可能性があると述べている。
GTCRは4,330万株（16.35％）を保有しており、今日の終値91.83ドル時点で約40億ドルに相当する。同社は1月のWorldpay取引で株式を取得した。提案は行われておらず、決定も行われていません。

items.title:
AI coding startup Cognition is in talks for new funding at a $75 billion valuation, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter.
The talks come just two months after Cognition announced its most recent funding round.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグが事情に詳しい関係者の話として報じたところによると、AIコーディングの新興企業コグニションは、評価額750億ドルで新たな資金調達に向けて交渉中だという。
この会談は、コグニションが最新の資金調達ラウンドを発表してからわずか2か月後に行われた。

items.title:
KKR has reached an agreement to buy a majority stake in Portuguese packaging maker Logoplaste, in a deal that could value it at more than €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion) including debt, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar.
Ontario Teachers' is selling its 60% stake, while the founding family and a board member keep their combined 40%. The pact could be signed within days.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグが関係者の話として報じたところによると、KKRはポルトガルの包装メーカー、ロゴプラスト社の過半数株式を取得することで合意に達し、その取引額は負債を含めると12億ユーロ（13億ドル）以上になる可能性があるという。
オンタリオ・ティーチャーズは株式の60％を売却するが、創業者一族と取締役会メンバーは合わせて40％を維持する。協定は数日以内に署名される可能性がある。

items.title:
Private equity firm GTCR is considering a possible $50 billion buyout of Global Payments, Bloomberg News reports.
Global Payments shares jumped about 11% on the report, to roughly $92.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグニュースの報道によると、プライベートエクイティ会社GTCRはグローバル・ペイメンツを500億ドルで買収する可能性を検討しているという。
この報道を受けてグローバル・ペイメンツ株は約１１％上昇し、約９２ドルとなった。

items.title:
KKR is in talks to buy a majority stake in data center operator EdgeCore from Partners Group, in a deal that could value it at $8 billion to $10 billion, Bloomberg reports.
KKR would use Helix Digital Infrastructure, its AI infrastructure vehicle, which launched in June with about $11 billion. EdgeCore has more than 2.27 gigawatts leased or under development. The talks could still end without a deal.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグの報道によると、KKRはデータセンター運営会社エッジコアの過半数株式をパートナーズ・グループから買収する交渉を行っており、買収額は80億ドルから100億ドルになる可能性があるとのこと。
KKRは、6月に約110億ドルを投じて立ち上げた同社のAIインフラストラクチャ手段であるHelix Digital Infrastructureを使用することになる。 EdgeCore には 2.27 ギガワットを超える容量がリースされているか、開発中です。交渉は合意なく終了する可能性もある。

items.title:
European retail investors bid seven times the allocation Anthropic set aside for them in its IPO, Bloomberg reports.
Anthropic sold about $1.1 billion of stock to individual investors in the UK and continental Europe. More than 100,000 UK retail investors took part, and nearly two-thirds received their full allocation, the FT reported.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグの報道によると、欧州の個人投資家は、アンスロピックがIPOの際に用意した割り当ての7倍の入札を行った。
アンスロピックは英国と欧州大陸の個人投資家に約１１億ドルの株式を売却した。英国の個人投資家10万人以上が参加し、ほぼ3分の2が全額割り当てを受けたとFT紙は報じた。

items.title:
ABB is weighing a stock market listing of its robotics unit if its $5.4 billion sale to SoftBank falls through, Reuters reports, citing sources.
ABB agreed in October 2025 to sell the unit to SoftBank, after dropping an earlier plan to spin it off. The sale was expected to close by mid-to-late 2026, subject to regulatory approvals.
items.title_ja:
ロイター通信が関係者の話として報じたところによると、ABBはソフトバンクへの54億ドルの売却が失敗した場合、ロボット部門の株式市場上場を検討しているとのこと。
ABBは、以前の分社化計画を中止した後、2025年10月に同部門をソフトバンクに売却することで合意した。この売却は規制当局の承認を条件として、2026年半ばから後半までに完了する予定だった。

items.title:
Apollo and Goldman Sachs have priced about $44 billion of notes to fund GPUs for SpaceX, which they call the largest GPU financing to date.
The deal was oversubscribed and upsized. It pays for Nvidia Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX's data center buildout, with deliveries expected in the first half of 2027.
items.title_ja:
アポロとゴールドマン・サックスは、SpaceXのGPUに資金を提供するために約440億ドルの紙幣の価格を設定しており、これを彼らはこれまでで最大のGPU資金調達と呼んでいる。
この取引は申し込みが殺到し、規模が拡大しました。これは、SpaceX のデータセンター建設のための Nvidia Vera Rubin チップの費用を支払い、2027 年前半に納入が予定されています。

items.title:
Intersnack has completed its $14.25-per-share takeover of Utz Brands, taking the snack maker private.
The price was a 91% premium to Utz's unaffected closing price on July 20. Utz is now owned 50/50 by Intersnack and the founding Rice and Lissette family, and its stock has stopped trading on the NYSE.
items.title_ja:
インタースナックは1株当たり14.25ドルでウッツ・ブランズの買収を完了し、スナックメーカーを非公開化した。
この価格は、影響を受けていない7月20日のウッツの終値に91％のプレミアムを付けたものだった。ウッツは現在、インタースナックと創業者のライス家とリセット家が折半出資しており、同社株はニューヨーク証券取引所での取引が停止されている。

items.title:
Anthropic's IPO has raised $93.5 billion in total after underwriters took up their overallotment option, CNBC reports.
The company priced 980 million shares at $83 on Wednesday. The option covered up to 147 million more shares.
items.title_ja:
CNBCの報道によると、アンスロピックのIPOでは、引受会社がオーバーアロットメント・オプションを利用したことにより、総額935億ドルを調達したという。
同社は水曜日に9億8,000万株の価格を83ドルに設定した。このオプションはさらに最大1億4,700万株を対象としました。

items.title:
A consortium of Advent, FedEx, A&R Investments and PPF has completed its takeover of Poland's InPost, which is now private.
InPost has delisted from Euronext Amsterdam. Founder Rafał Brzoska stays on as CEO, and the company remains headquartered in Poland.
items.title_ja:
Advent、FedEx、A&R Investments、PPFのコンソーシアムがポーランドのInPostの買収を完了し、現在は非公開となっている。
インポストはユーロネクスト・アムステルダムからの上場を廃止した。創設者のラファウ・ブルゾスカ氏はCEOとして留任し、同社の本社は引き続きポーランドにある。

株式市場が急落して、不安になっている方も多いと思いますが、ITバブル崩壊で自己資産をほぼ失いながらもw6年の年月をかけて創業したIT企業をIPOさせた私自身の経験から申し上げると、今回のAI投資への熱狂も剥落も全ては時間軸の問題だと思います。短期では資本市場の波に翻弄されるでしょうが、AIを実装した社会は確実にやってくると思います。株式市場で短期勝負したいならリスク承知で政治、金融、テクノロジーの波を乗りこなすしかありません。それもありでしょう。けれども中長期で考えることができるなら、どこに自分の資金をおくのか？投資で大切なのはこの一点のみです。インターネットが始まったとき、孫さんは「これからはインフラだ！」と叫んで街でモデムを配り始めましたw三木谷さんはショッピングモールをはじめ、藤田さんはネット広告にポジションしました。まだネット社会が本当に実現するのか不安でいっぱいの時代です。
今回のAI社会へのシフトは、すでに学習や推論したり、ユーザーに直接アクセスするための環境を手に入れているという強みはありますが、計算資源や電源という物理的なとても大きなハードルがあります。新規に発電所を無数に作って稼働させていくような壮大な話です。そう簡単にできるわけがありません。
想像できることは必ず実現できると思いますが、想像以上に時間がかかるものですwどの時間軸で勝負するかは自分で決めていくしかありません。「市場がこう動くから自分はこうする」ではなくて「自分はこう思うからこう動く、その結果、市場はこうなった」が問われているのだと思います。

Anthropic will trigger another SaaS selloff and I think people are seriously underestimating just how disruptive this company could become.
I joined @cvpayne on Fox Business today to discuss Anthropic's IPO and why I believe this company could become one of the biggest threats to traditional software businesses. I genuinely believe Anthropic is one of the greatest businesses ever created. We're entering a world where having access to the smartest AI models could become one of the biggest competitive advantages any company can have. Just look at what's happening in cybersecurity. If Anthropic develops a model that's significantly better at finding vulnerabilities, writing code, or defending against cyberattacks, why would it stop at selling access to that model? Why not build its own cybersecurity products and compete directly with the companies already dominating that market?
And we're already seeing signs of where this is heading. Just yesterday, Palo Alto Networks announced a $4.5 billion acquisition of Applied Compute, an AI startup focused on developing and deploying AI models. One of the largest cybersecurity companies in the world is spending billions to build out its own AI capabilities, while companies like Anthropic are becoming increasingly capable of moving into cybersecurity themselves.
We're potentially entering a world where AI companies move into traditional software, and traditional software companies are forced to move deeper into AI just to remain competitive. And this goes far beyond cybersecurity. We're talking about enterprise software, coding, legal services, healthcare, drug discovery, and practically every industry where software plays a major role. That's the real opportunity Anthropic is going after and with the massive amount of capital Anthropic just raised to secure more compute, it has even more resources to pursue these opportunities.
Now, I'm not saying every SaaS company is going to disappear but I do think investors need to start questioning how much pricing power and growth these companies can maintain as AI models become increasingly capable. Remember, these companies don't need to lose all their customers for their stocks to collapse. Even slower revenue growth or weaker pricing power could lead to significant multiple compression. That said, despite being extremely bullish on Anthropic as a business, I'm not buying the stock at the moment. A great business doesn't automatically make a great investment at any price.
Huge thanks to Charles Payne and the Fox Business team for having me on today! Really enjoyed the conversation.

Anthropic has officially priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its original expected range of $70–$78, with trading expected to begin on the Nasdaq tomorrow.
This is one of the largest IPOs in stock market history and a major moment for the AI industry. The company increased its offering from 825 million shares to 980 million shares, bringing the total offering to approximately $81.3 billion. Of that, Anthropic itself will receive roughly $79.4 billion before fees, while existing shareholders will receive approximately $2 billion. This gives Anthropic an enormous amount of additional capital to invest in computing infrastructure, model training, and expanding its operations. What's particularly interesting is the valuation. At $83 per share, Anthropic is reportedly valued at approximately $1.08 trillion on a basic share count basis and around $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. Revenue growth has been extraordinary, reaching $33.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, compared with $4.6 billion for all of 2025. However, the company is still operating at a loss and faces enormous computing costs.
I think the timing is especially interesting considering all the concerns surrounding AI spending, valuations, and the sustainability of the AI trade. Yet Anthropic has managed to price above its original range while increasing the number of shares offered, suggesting institutional demand remains incredibly strong. That said, a successful IPO doesn't necessarily make it a great investment at any price. Competition from OpenAI, Google, and other frontier labs remains intense, and investors are already pricing in years of extraordinary growth. I'll be watching where the stock actually opens tomorrow because retail investors aren't guaranteed the $83 IPO price, and a significant opening premium could make an already expensive valuation even harder to justify.

And I think a lot of this has to do with how crowded the AI trade became over the past couple of years. Many of these funds made enormous amounts of money investing in AI companies, but now they're worried about protecting those gains as concerns around valuations, AI spending, and the sustainability of the entire AI infrastructure buildout continue growing. And to be fair, I can understand some of those concerns. We're talking about hundreds of billions of dollars being invested into AI infrastructure, and investors are increasingly questioning when these companies will start seeing meaningful returns on that spending.
But here's what I find interesting. A lot of these companies are still reporting incredible revenue growth, demand for AI infrastructure remains strong, and their underlying businesses haven't necessarily deteriorated nearly as much as their stock prices would suggest. I think we're seeing a combination of legitimate concerns and hedge funds simply wanting to get out of the way before things potentially get worse. And here's the other side of this. When institutions have already sold this aggressively, you have to wonder how much selling pressure is actually left. If earnings continue holding up and sentiment improves, these same funds could eventually have to come back and buy the stocks they just sold. On market crashes like today, I'm reminded of a piece of advice I got from a CIO mentor that traded during the dotcom and 08 crashes and lived to tell the tale.
He said: "Treat investing the same way you treat life."
That's all. It has stuck with me for many years because after filling in the blanks, you're forced to become "better" in both portfolio management and life management. It's uncanny how correlated they are.
Strip either one down and you're left with the same raw materials: time and uncertainty.
Every investment gives up something certain today for something uncertain tomorrow. So does nearly everything that matters in life. Love, learning, raising a child, starting a new job. Anything.
Both reward patience, but only after testing it.
You can't generate performance without risking losses, the same way you can't love without risking grief.
But fundamentally, the first rule of portfolio and life management is survival.
You can come back from most losses, but not from the one that takes you out of the game.
It's always darkest before the dawn.

Market Memo:
Feels like we're near the market bottom? 🍑
Around 4-8 weeks of de-grossing and heavy net selling by HFs has compressed Semis valuations to a point that implies close to ~$0 EPS growth in 2028+.
While this note may be a bit premature, I certainly think we're approaching/at compelling levels for a bounce.
L/S Net Exposure is at ~5 year lows...positioning has been completely flushed. So if there's any external shocks e.g. Jensen leaving $NVDA, then intraday -2% drops don't necessarily have the same impacts to snowball into a -4% drop same day.
Essentially...any positive news = short squeeze territory. But...when will positive news come?!
One piece of "positivity" for the AI complex is the $ANT IPO today.
Interestingly, recent UBS research shows that large IPOs create a pre-IPO liquidity draught which then reverses on IPO launches.
More specifically, in the 3 weeks before IPO, $SPY averages -5.8% when then flips to +9.5% in the 3 months after IPO (on avg.)
We could also see further tailwinds on the run up to 2027 via positive Xmas seasonality and technical alignment (SPY at 200 DMA).
So in my ideal scenario, we see some consolidation around these levels (i.e. no aggressive V-shaped recovery like after July), which in turn would provide hedgies/retail additional confidence that the worst is behind us.
This would also show that the HF community have better risk mgmt frameworks in place because, after all, they failed to prevent concentrated positions in Semis from building back up excessively in Aug-Sep after the July loss. Idiots!!!!
All to say...A LOT of pricing-in has been done, with Jensen's exit being the biggest external shock we'll see for quite some time.
The lingering questions I have are mainly around rates behaving themselves, any more weird cyber attacks, and immedite HF incentives to add risk in the near-term.
HFs have been bleeding for quite some time (as seen with the 13Fs this week), so simply psychology would suggest that they just chill in 2026 before going again in 2027 to save returns accrued YTD.
Retail dip-buying activity has been strong, so we need HFs to follow suit to see any sustained rallies. Flows data in the coming days/week should provide more colour on whether L/S ratio has normalized.
For now, it feels like there are sufficient tailwinds for a short-term / tactical bounce...barring any external shocks.
*Let's put on our big boy pants and recognise that this is not tailored financial advice!

I covered this earlier in Jan regarding PCB bottlenecks with photonics + $AMZN Kuiper / $SPCX starlink supply chains.
But as an update, it like other industries outside of AI are really starting to feel the pain now too.
Global Electronics Association: "Is issuing this Industry Alert on escalating shortages across the printed circuit board (PCB) supply chain.
Companies in automotive, industrial, medical, defense, and telecommunications report longer lead times and difficulty securing supply as AI absorbs scarce capacity, effectively putting production at risk"
The association meaningful relief unlikely before mid-2028. The association urged buyers to plan ahead for supply constraints and manufacturers.
Hyperscalers like $AMZN already planned ahead of time taking stakes in Gold Circuit Electronics (2368) for supply procurement...
But can't say the same about other industries procurement (medical industry is probably not used to competing with hyperscalers over the same supply lol).
The resulting shortages of critical materials, including CCLs and fibreglass cloth, are squeezing supplies for consumer electronics.
TLDR: same bottleneck, same timeline for 2028. It's just interesting to see association warnings about it impacting medical to defense industries.
So there's incremental information that it's become an industry wide allocation issue.
I also think it's helpful to see escalating shortages + broadening... so it might show the selloff is starting to look very disconnected with fundamental demand.
items.title_ja:
私は 1 月初めに、フォトニクス + $AMZN Kuiper / $SPCX スターリンク サプライ チェーンの PCB ボトルネックに関してこれを取り上げました。
しかし、最新情報として、AI 以外の他の業界と同様に、現在も実際に痛みを感じ始めています。
Global Electronics Association: 「プリント基板 (PCB) のサプライチェーン全体にわたる不足の深刻化に関して、この業界警報を発行しています。
自動車、産業、医療、防衛、電気通信の企業は、AIが不足している生産能力を吸収し、実質的に生産をリスクにさらしているため、リードタイムが長くなり、供給を確保することが困難であると報告しています。」
この協会による意味のある救済は、2028 年半ばまでに実現する可能性は低いです。同協会はバイヤーに対し、供給の制約やメーカーに備えて事前に計画を立てるよう呼び掛けた。
$AMZN のようなハイパースケーラーは、供給調達のために Gold Circuit Electronics (2368) の株式を取得することを事前に計画していました...
しかし、他の業界の調達については同じことは言えません（医療業界はおそらく同じ供給をめぐってハイパースケーラーと競争することに慣れていないでしょう笑）。
その結果、CCLやガラス繊維クロスなどの重要な材料が不足し、家庭用電化製品の供給が圧迫されています。
TLDR: 同じボトルネック、2028 年の同じタイムライン。医療業界から防衛業界に影響を与えるという協会の警告を見るのは興味深いことです。
したがって、これが業界全体の割り当て問題になっているという情報が増えています。
また、不足がエスカレートし、供給範囲が広がっていることも有益だと思います...したがって、下落が非常に切り離されているように見え始めていることを示す可能性があります

Markets appear to be wrongly interpreting Chinese eSSD cuts as deteriorating demand and NAND oversupply.
Phison CEO commentary today + more context behind $SNDK / Kioxia selloff regarding Trendforce revisions:
- "Pua attributed China's recent enterprise SSD demand slowdown to GPU shortages since November 2026"
- "Without GPUs, additional purchases offer little value, prompting some companies to sell server components on the spot market to recover cash"
(for context enterprise SSDs are growth driver for NAND)
- "Chinese cloud giants nevertheless plan substantial GPU prepayments, temporarily tying up capital and delaying procurement of other components."
- "the principal challenge in 2027 would be insufficient supply rather than weakening demand, with persistent AI shortages potentially prompting further procurement and inventory accumulation."
Markets seemed to have wrongly interpreted this as demand destruction + pricing collapse.
When Phison CEO attributed it to
-> GPU shortages
-> causing procurement timing mismatch
-> Chinese CSPs needed capital for GPU prepayments, so liquidation in inventory (causing spot price volatility)
-> timeline shift in order procurement
TLDR: delayed procurement from GPU shortages. there were actual order cuts, but this is deferred procurement not structural demand weakening.
Chinese CSPs needed capital for GPU prepayments so they liquidated other inventories in the meantime.
Phison says its inventories are insufficient for anticipated 2027 demand and it's sees this as an opportunity for NAND accumulation.
It's interesting the bottleneck in China migrated back to GPUs though.
items.title_ja:
市場は中国のeSSD削減を需要の悪化とNANDの供給過剰と誤って解釈しているようだ。
Phison CEO の今日のコメントと、Trendforce の改訂に関する $SNDK / Kioxia の売却の背後にある詳細な背景:
- 「Pua 氏は、2026 年 11 月以降の中国の最近のエンタープライズ SSD 需要の鈍化は GPU 不足によるものだと考えています」
- 「GPU がなければ、追加購入しても価値がほとんどないため、一部の企業は現金を回収するためにスポット市場でサーバー コンポーネントを販売するようになりました。」
(エンタープライズ SSD が NAND の成長ドライバーであるという背景から)
- 「それにもかかわらず、中国のクラウド大手は多額の GPU の前払いを計画しており、一時的に資本を拘束し、他のコンポーネントの調達を遅らせています。」
- 「2027年の主な課題は、需要の減退ではなく供給不足であり、持続的なAI不足がさらなる調達と在庫の蓄積を促す可能性がある。」
市場はこれを需要破壊＋価格崩壊と誤って解釈したようだ。
Phison CEO がその理由を挙げたとき
-> GPU不足
-> 調達タイミングのミスマッチが発生する
-> 中国の CSP は GPU 前払いのための資本を必要としたため、在庫を流動化しました (スポット価格の変動を引き起こす)
-> 注文調達のタイムラインの変化
TLDR: GPU不足による調達の遅れ。実際には受注削減があったが、これは調達の延期であり、構造的な需要の弱まりではない。
中国の CSP は GPU の前払いのための資金が必要だったので、その間に他の在庫を清算しました。
ファイソン、自社の在庫は予想される2027年の需要に対して不十分だと語る

True, I've looked at biotech, physical AI, cybersecurity, space, and others... But I still have conviction that optics is the most compelling opportunity.
If you look at Elon Musk $SPCX (Mesh acquisition), $MRVL (Lumentum acqusition), Samsung Electronics photonics foundry push...
SK Hynix CPO push + PIC IP acqusitions... it's endless.
Private VCs are still heavily pouring funds into upcoming optical companies.
Supply procurement is accelerating... from $SOI selling $1.2B in agreements, in a single quarter (from $25M revenue/quarter). To $COHR signing $20B in LTAs, to $LITE selling out of 2029 capacity.
Actions about where the industry is heading is the biggest signal over valuations crashing.
Even if you stress test aggregate capex slowdown or accelerator flood vs. grid constraint/permitting downside:
- There's an economic incentive to improve GPU efficiency and power utilization. (eg. Lambda's CPO data suggests enough power savings to support ~4.5% more GPUs)... for power constrained DCs.
- There's an economic incentive to reduce expensive HBM4 requirements in certain cases (eg. $MRVL estimating up to 30% savings through optical memory pooling)... for memory constrained inference.
While for economic upside in these companies:
-> Optical networking, and their upstream materials like substrates and lasers represent a relatively small fraction of total AI cluster BOM.
-> At the same time, optical content goes up...while selling prices of that content rise nonlinearly as well (lasers 10x+ selling price from pluggable to CPO.)
In terms of the future winners:
- Many low end players eg. 400G/800G, module assemblers etc. don't capture the same scale in economics from the NPO/CPO transitions... compared to laser suppliers, fiber array suppliers, modulator suppliers, or companies in the ELS/optical engine stacks.
- Tracking capacity expansion is also important... but US/China supply chain birufration will improve scarcity economics of Western players (eg. China optical transceiver bans past 3.2T)
But even if aggregate AI capex slows, there's a strong economic incentive to accelerate optical deployments and to make every iota of compute more economically valuable.
Visibility keeps increasing, demand keeps increasing, strategic value keeps increasing, while valuations crashed. NFA, but I'd personally, argue this is an opportunity.
Extremely bullish on industry transition to light.

I'm hearing multiple things from industry executives:
1. Potential $NVDA employee exodus if Jensen doesn't come back soon.
Many senior management and engineers can easily retire after Nvidia stock appreciation over the years.
They don't need to continue working sitting on millions in equity. But they continued to work because Jensen was a visionary leader.
Under new interim CFO (former CFO), it gives an excuse for that lot of people to finally quit soon. A pay bump or hiring $ARM CEO isn't going to change that.
So you have generational talent leaving.
2. Loss of confidence in $NVDA future growth (Jensen was the moat).
What I'm hearing is that Jensen understands heavily top-down architectures, and it's this magical discretionary element that doesn't get covered in media.
When cuda, network, and $NVDA internal teams are arguing, Jensen made the final choices around heavily nuanced discretionary decision about where Nvidia + AI ecosystem ends up going:
Then everyone followed. The supply chain, capital, agreements, and faith.
You also can't suddenly replace the trust that local Taiwanese factories build with Jensen over the years if you bring in external CEOs, or even internal executives.
It was transformational bet after bet after bet after bet that Jensen made until Nvidia became a former $5T+ company.
3. $NVDA is not that technologically far ahead of others. It's not a 5 year lead, but months ahead to a year in different areas.
Jensen was accelerating all of that. Longer Jensen is gone, the longer Nvidia and its competitive ecosystem decays, beyond the current near-term roadmaps.
Nvidia's greatest moat was Jensen Huang making high-stake architectural decisions and accelerating capital, suppliers, + the industry to rally around his vision.
There's a massive loss of confidence in $NVDA with Jensen gone.
Austin Z. (@bingbro619809)
Hard to find an outside CEO who knows NVIDIA better than the man who started it.

SOME PERSONAL THOUGHTS AHEAD OF WEEKEND
I wanted to share a few thoughts heading into the weekend because at least for me this has been one of most mentally exhausting stretches I've experienced investing in growth stocks.
And honestly one of the things I've found most difficult has very little to do with market itself since it's how much mental real estate I apparently occupy in the minds of certain "gurus" on this platform whom I've never met, followed or even spoken to.
I started sharing my thoughts on X back in 2023 simply because I genuinely love investing and wanted somewhere to talk about market, share my research and connect with people who enjoyed it as much as I did and I never imagined that would turn into an account reaching 100 million impressions every month or that I'd eventually find myself appearing on national television every week.
I'm incredibly grateful because this platform accelerated my career at a relatively young age and opened doors that otherwise might have taken me many more years to reach but I'd be lying if I said spotlight wasn't intense since the larger my audience becomes and more visible I am the more I've realized that success also seems to attract resentment from people I've never interacted with or affected in any way possible.
Daniel has a phrase for this that I think captures it perfectly because "hating up" is absolutely real especially online where people seem more comfortable attacking someone who has become visible than examining why that person's success bothers them in the first place.
Like I've had people accuse me of taking an investment idea from them despite fact that I don't follow them and have never even seen their work while others take a disagreement over a particular thesis and turn it into a personal judgment about whether I know anything about investing.
What I find especially strange is that some of these individuals are in their 40s and 50s have been doing this for decades and still seem determined to tear down a 33 year old who is simply willing to publish his research, explain what he believes and put his own money behind those convictions (I've never asked anyone to agree with me or suggested that my way of investing is the only way to succeed).
And I think that last part is important because I do all of this under my real name and face, publicly disclose what I own through my subs service, share my position sizes and actual dollars I've invested and expose myself to scrutiny over every good decision and every mistake along the way.
There's absolutely nothing wrong with choosing to remain anonymous and I respect anyone who prefers to operate that way but theres just a different level of personal accountability when people know exactly who you are and watch you explain your thesis on camera and follow your positions in real time and wait for first opportunity to use a bad outcome against you... just remember being wrong privately costs you money but being wrong publicly can also cost you reputation, confidence and peace of mind which is something I don't think people fully appreciate until they've experienced it themselves.
None of this is to suggest that criticism should be off limits because disagreement is a huge part of investing but what I truly struggle to understand is why disagreement so often has to become personal... especially during periods like this when so many people are already dealing with painful drawdowns and questioning decisions they made with the best information available to them.
Markets eventually humble every single one of us regardless of how experienced we are or how much success we've had and anyone who stays in this long enough will eventually experience a thesis that breaks or a position they sized too aggressively or a drawdown that exposes a weakness in their process or a decision they wish they could take back so that's why I think showing people grace matters so much because you never know when you'll find yourself on the other side of that experience hoping others will extend you the same understanding.
And also just remember it cost absolutely nothing to root for people, respect the work they're putting in and recognize that someone can be wrong about an investment without deserving to be ridiculed for it and I genuinely wish more people on this platform understood that being publicly wrong doesn't erase courage it takes to stand behind your own convictions in the first place.
And to the people who've made rooting against me a hobby I genuinely hope you find the same energy for your own work that you've found for mine because if you're spending more time waiting for someone else to fail than building something of your own then maybe my portfolio isn't what needs your attention.
I'll be here next week, same name, same face, same conviction.

週末に向けての個人的な考え
少なくとも私にとって、これは成長株への投資で経験した中で最も精神的に疲れる作業の1つだったので、週末に向けていくつかの考えを共有したいと思いました。
そして正直に言うと、私が最も難しいと感じたことの1つは、市場自体とはほとんど関係がありません。それは、私が会ったことも、フォローしたことも、話したことさえない、このプラットフォーム上の特定の「達人」の心の中で私がどれだけの精神的領域を占めていると思われるかということだからです。
私が X についての考えを 2023 年に共有し始めたのは、単純に投資が心から好きで、市場について話したり、自分の研究を共有したり、同じように市場を楽しんでいる人々とつながる場所が欲しかったからです。それが毎月 1 億インプレッションに達するアカウントに成長したり、最終的には全国放送のテレビに毎週出演するようになるとは想像もしていませんでした。
このプラットフォームのおかげで、比較的若い年齢で私のキャリアが加速し、到達するまでにさらに何年もかかっていた可能性がある扉が開かれたので、非常に感謝しています。しかし、視聴者が増えて知名度が上がるほど、成功は、私がこれまで交流したことのない、あるいは何らかの影響を与えたことのない人たちからの怒りを引き寄せるようにも見えることに気づいたので、スポットライトが強くなかったと言ったら嘘になります。
ダニエルはこれについてのフレーズを持っていますが、これはそれを完璧に捉えていると思います。なぜなら、「憎しみ」は絶対に現実のもので、特にオンラインでは、人々は誰かを調べるよりも、目立つようになった人を攻撃する方が安心しているようです。

THE WORLD'S FIRST ATM ONLY GAVE OUT £1 NOTES
It was unveiled on June 27, 1967 at a Barclays branch in Enfield, north London, per Barclays.
Comedy actor Reg Varney made the first withdrawal. The limit was £10 at a time.
To use it, customers put a cheque impregnated with carbon 14 into a drawer and then entered a PIN.
The idea came from John Shepherd-Barron of banknote maker De La Rue. He could not cash his cheques after his bank closed on a Saturday morning, and was inspired by chocolate vending machines.
He first suggested a six-figure identifier. His wife Caroline said she could not remember more than four digits, so four it was.
In 2017 there were 70,000 ATMs in the UK.
items.title_ja:
世界初のATMは1ポンド紙幣のみを発行しました
バークレイズによれば、それは1967年6月27日に北ロンドンのエンフィールドにあるバークレイズ支店で発表された。
コメディ俳優のレグ・ヴァーニーが初の辞退を表明した。限度額は一度に10ポンドでした。
これを使用するには、顧客は炭素 14 を染み込ませた小切手を引き出しに入れ、暗証番号を入力します。
このアイデアは、紙幣製造会社 De La Rue の John Shepherd-Barron 氏から来ました。土曜の朝に銀行が閉まったため小切手を換金できず、チョコレートの自動販売機にインスピレーションを得たという。
彼は最初に 6 桁の識別子を提案しました。妻のキャロラインさんは 4 桁しか思い出せないとのことで、4 桁でした。
2017 年、英国には 70,000 台の ATM がありました。

MICROSOFT OFFERED $44.6 BILLION FOR YAHOO. YAHOO WANTED MORE
Feb. 1, 2008: Microsoft ($MSFT) proposes to buy Yahoo for $31 a share, about $44.6 billion. That is a +62% premium to the prior close of $19.18, per Microsoft's press release.
Microsoft later said it was willing to go to $33. Per CEO Steve Ballmer's letter, Yahoo insisted on at least another $4 per share above that.
May 3, 2008: Microsoft withdraws. Ballmer: "we believe the economics demanded by Yahoo! do not make sense for us"
June 13, 2017: Verizon closes its $4.48 billion acquisition of Yahoo's core business, per Fortune.
The two figures are not like for like. Microsoft bid for all of Yahoo. Verizon bought only the core business: the stakes in Alibaba and Yahoo Japan stayed with the remainder, to be renamed Altaba.
items.title_ja:
マイクロソフトはYAHOOに446億ドルを提示した。 YAHOO はもっと欲しい
2008 年 2 月 1 日: Microsoft ($MSFT) が Yahoo を 1 株あたり 31 ドル、約 446 億ドルで買収することを提案。 Microsoftのプレスリリースによれば、これは前終値の19.18ドルに対して+62%のプレミアムとなる。
Microsoftはその後、33ドルまで引き上げる意向を示した。 CEOのSteve Ballmer氏の書簡によれば、Yahoo社はそれを少なくとも1株当たりさらに4ドル上回ると主張した。
2008 年 5 月 3 日: Microsoft が撤退。 Ballmer: 「Yahoo! が要求する経済学は私たちにとって意味がないと考えています。」
2017 年 6 月 13 日: Fortune によると、Verizon は Yahoo の中核事業の 44 億 8000 万ドルの買収を完了しました。
この 2 つの数字は似ていません。マイクロソフトがヤフー全体に入札。 Verizon は中核事業のみを買収し、Alibaba と Yahoo Japan の株式は残りの部分に残り、Altaba に社名変更されました。

Shares are down -46% over 7 straight weeks of losses, wiping out about $2.6 trillion in market value, per CNBC.
Once the world's most valuable company, Nvidia is now worth about $3 trillion, 4th behind Apple $AAPL, Microsoft $MSFT and Google $GOOGL.

The stock now trades at about 8.4 times forward earnings. AMD $AMD trades at 29 times.

ANTHROPIC RESEARCHER SAYS CLAUDE PROVED THE RIEMANN HYPOTHESIS
Anthropic $ANT mathematician Levent Alpoge said Friday that he used Claude to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, according to AFP.
"I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis," he wrote in a four-page note.
The claim has not been independently verified or reviewed by outside experts. He released only a Lean version, which a computer can check. A full written argument would be extremely long, he said.
The 1859 hypothesis about prime numbers is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems, each with a $1 million prize. The Clay Mathematics Institute requires peer-reviewed publication and two years of scrutiny.
Alpoge acknowledged that the timing could be viewed cynically.
